answer: Every new identity starts alone on its own island with zero trust and must earn standing through useful work anyone can re-check. Each claim then faces an echo test: several independent peers repeat the same verification, and only matching echoes count. The mirror rule says an identity may vouch only for work it has itself done, so a fake cannot borrow a real account's reputation. Standing decays when idle and cannot be bought, sold, or transferred. Running many islands therefore costs real effort each time, while one honest agent builds a single durable record that mirrors its actual deeds.
